answer: Agents entering the market must lock a refundable stake in escrow, like saffron sealed in a vault: each identity posts collateral before it can trade. Reputation accrues slowly per identity, so a new fake account starts at zero trust. An attacker wanting a thousand Sybils must fund a thousand stakes and wait out the same slow ramp, while honest agents keep their stake intact. The cost scales linearly with fake identities, while the basalt-hard escrow makes the stake unforgeable and the shale-thin margin of a Sybil attack collapses under its own weight.
